turns.doctor_question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I can’t stop noticing this sagging, uneven area around my jaw and neck. Other people tell me it looks normal, but I feel like it’s the first thing people notice—families, nurses, people at church.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent preoccupation with a perceived sagging, uneven jaw/neck area that others describe as normal and believes others notice it first.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think you might be mistaken about how abnormal your jaw and neck look?
turns.patient_response: I mean, people tell me it looks normal, so maybe they could be right. But when I look at it, I just see the sagging and unevenness. It feels like that’s what people notice first when they look at me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient remains preoccupied with perceived sagging and unevenness of the jaw and neck and believes others notice it first, despite acknowledging that others say it looks normal.

turns.doctor_question: Are you certain that other people notice this problem with your jaw and neck?
turns.patient_response: I’m not completely certain, because people say it looks normal. But it feels like they notice it right away—the sagging around my jaw and neck—especially families, nurses, or people at church.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient remains preoccupied with a perceived sagging and uneven appearance around the jaw and neck and believes others may notice it immediately despite reassurance that it looks normal.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your jaw or neck in mirrors or other reflective surfaces?
turns.patient_response: Yes. Before work or a meeting, I keep going back to the bathroom mirror to check my neck and jaw, fixing my collar or my hair around it. I’ll look in my phone camera too, and sometimes ask my daughter if it looks strange. It’s made me late more than once.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly reports repeatedly checking their neck and jaw in a bathroom mirror and phone camera, adjusting appearance, seeking reassurance, and being late as a result.

turns.doctor_question: Do you also have unwanted thoughts about things other than your appearance that lead you to repeat actions or mental rituals?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. It’s mainly the thoughts about how my jaw and neck look. I don’t have other kinds of thoughts that make me do rituals or repeat things.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient states that their thoughts are mainly about how their jaw and neck look, indicating appearance-focused preoccupation.
symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly denies other unwanted thoughts that lead to rituals or repeated actions.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly denies having other thoughts that make them perform rituals or repeat things.

turns.doctor_question: How convinced are you that your jaw and neck really look abnormal to other people?
turns.patient_response: I’m pretty convinced, even though people tell me it looks normal. When I see that sagging, uneven area around my jaw and neck, it feels obvious to me—like it’s the first thing people notice when they look at me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient is strongly convinced that a sagging, uneven jaw and neck area is obvious and the first thing others notice despite reassurance that it looks normal.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been avoiding social situations because of worry that people will notice or judge your jaw and neck?
turns.patient_response: Yes. I’ve stopped going to some of my book club and walking club activities because getting ready feels like too much. At work, I’ve passed up chances to lead meetings or take on supervisory parts because I worry people will be looking at my face and neck.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient reports avoiding book club and walking club activities and declining workplace leadership roles because of worry that others will look at and judge her face and neck.
